title: ThermEval — A Structured Benchmark for Evaluation of Vision-Language Models on Thermal Imagery
venue: KDD 2026 (Accepted, Poster — Datasets & Benchmarks Track, A* Conference)
abstract: Developed a large-scale benchmark of 70,000+ VQA samples across 25 open and closed-source Vision-Language Models (0.3B–235B parameters, including Phi, Qwen-VL, and Gemini) to systematically evaluate reasoning capabilities on thermal imagery. Built an end-to-end evaluation pipeline with an LLM-based output parser validated on 1,200 gold samples (>98% human agreement). Uncovered that VLMs reliably identify thermal images as a modality but consistently fail at temperature-grounded reasoning by defaulting to language priors (e.g., assuming 'normal' body temperature regardless of pixel color). Proved that this grounding issue is not solved merely by scale, as failures persist up to 235B parameters. Demonstrated that fine-tuning with a LoRA-tuned 8B model closes much of the gap, approaching human performance.
